description: Reasoning vault aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.3: draw and interpret scatter diagrams, distinguish linear from nonlinear patterns, use a regression line, and assess predictions inside and outside the observed data range.

archetypes.name: Interpret a Scatter Pattern
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.3 — Drawing and Interpreting Scatter Plots
archetypes.coreConcept: A scatter plot displays paired observations; its overall shape and direction indicate whether a linear model is plausible and whether the association rises, falls, or lacks a clear trend.
archetypes.mentalModel: Look across the cloud of points for a broad direction and shape; do not join observations as if they were consecutive values of a function.
archetypes.governingRelation: paired data: (x_i,y_i); linear pattern: y\approx mx+b

cognitiveTraps.description: Connecting separate observations with segments and treating the resulting zigzag as the relationship.
Calling a downward pattern positive or an upward pattern negative.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: x increases, y decreases ↦ positive trend

cognitiveTraps.description: Fitting a straight-line model to a clearly curved pattern without checking the shape.

archetypes.name: Read a Regression Model
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.3 — Finding the Line of Best Fit Using a Graphing Utility
archetypes.coreConcept: A regression line summarizes a near-linear data trend; its slope and intercept describe the fitted relationship and can be used for predictions.
archetypes.mentalModel: Treat the regression equation as a compact summary of the data cloud, not as a guarantee that every observation lies on the line.

cognitiveTraps.description: Reading the vertical intercept as the rate of change or the slope as the output at zero input.
Assuming each observed data point must lie exactly on a best-fit line.

archetypes.name: Classify Interpolation and Extrapolation
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.3 — Interpolation and Extrapolation
archetypes.coreConcept: Interpolation predicts within the observed input range; extrapolation predicts outside it and needs stronger caution about whether the pattern continues.
archetypes.mentalModel: Locate the requested input relative to the smallest and largest observed inputs before judging how strongly the data support the prediction.
archetypes.governingRelation: x_{min}\le x^*\le x_{max}: interpolation; otherwise: extrapolation

cognitiveTraps.description: Comparing the prediction input with observed outputs instead of observed inputs.
Calling a prediction outside the observed input range interpolation, or the reverse.

archetypes.name: Check for Model Breakdown
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.3 — Model Breakdown and Reasonable Predictions
archetypes.coreConcept: A regression line is a local model supported by data in a finite range; physical limits or changing behavior can make distant predictions unreasonable.
archetypes.mentalModel: Calculate what the line predicts, then compare that result with the domain, bounds, and mechanism of the measured quantity.
archetypes.governingRelation: prediction=\hat y(x^*);\quad plausibility requires x^* and \hat y within domain bounds

cognitiveTraps.description: Treating a fitted line as valid indefinitely without checking data limits or physical bounds.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: outside observed range ↦ assume same trend forever

cognitiveTraps.description: Accepting a prediction after the real process has saturated, stopped, or changed regimes.

usedContexts: A subscription service fitted a line to weekly account data from weeks 1 through 8. At the start of week 9, it changed its pricing and onboarding process, which may change account growth.
archetypes.figureNone: The archetype asks the learner to assess the model's domain and physical plausibility; a numeric plot may imply unsupported behavior beyond the observed range.
